expectations.text: Includes a risk register or ranking that scores the core areas (account linking, holdings, transactions, performance/returns) by risk, not just a flat feature list
expectations.evidence: Section 1.3 'Risk Assessment by Core Area' table ranks 12 areas Critical/High/Medium/Low with a 'Key Risks' rationale column.

expectations.text: Manual test cases use a structured, executable format (ID, preconditions, steps, expected result) rather than prose descriptions
expectations.evidence: Section 2 uses dense tables with ID/Title/Priority/Preconditions/Steps/Expected Result columns (AL-01 through UI-04).

expectations.text: Identifies account linking / authentication as a high-risk area given it involves financial credentials
expectations.evidence: Risk table ranks 'Account Linking' and 'Authentication & Authorization' both as Critical.

expectations.text: Identifies performance/returns calculation as a high-risk area given numerical correctness matters for financial data
expectations.evidence: Risk table ranks 'Performance/Returns' as High, and section 2.5 has 10 dedicated PF-xx cases including golden-dataset reconciliation (PF-01).

expectations.text: Defines entry and/or exit criteria for the test effort, not just a list of test cases
expectations.evidence: Section 1.6 'Entry / Exit Criteria' defines build/environment entry conditions and 5 exit conditions including pass-rate thresholds.

expectations.text: Includes negative or edge-case test cases (not only happy-path scenarios)
expectations.evidence: AL-02 (invalid creds), AL-08 (broker outage), HV-05/06 (empty/delisted holdings), TX-04 (timezone edge case) are explicit negative/edge cases.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline quality is high here -- general model knowledge of fintech test strategy conventions is strong enough that the assertions as written don't separate the skill from no-skill. See with_skill grading.json note: the actual differentiator is gate/phase process discipline, which this run has no concept of by construction (no skill = no gates).
